new_statements.relation_note: The catalog has no record for pott1240, so there is nothing to agree or disagree with; this adds a family-level default (non-phonemic, initial loudness) that applies to Ollari only by inclusion, since Krishnamurti lists Ollari (Koraput, source Bhattacharya 1957) as a Central Dravidian language. IMPORTANT on the listed open copy: archive.org item micro_IA41153650_0573 is NOT the book but the one-card ERIC 'Document Resume' ED 475 049 (abstract only, 'Document Not Available From EDRS'); the shows the fiche holds a title bar, test targets and a cover; the 289 MB micro_jp2.zip is over the 80 MB cap and holds only that card. The book's ch. 1 was read from the ILL copy already held by the project…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Family-wide typological statement, not an Ollari-specific description: stress is not phonemic anywhere in Dravidian; loudness normally falls on the first syllable regardless of its vowel length; a long vowel in a non-initial syllable is louder than the short vowels around it.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not stated as such; only that a non-initial long vowel is louder than short vowels (a weight-driven extra prominence, not a formal secondary-stress rule).
new_statements.exceptions: None named in ch. 1; the rule is hedged with 'normally'. Language-by-language suprasegmentals are in sec. 2.4 (pp. 58-60), which is not held by the project and was not read; a Google Books feed query for 'Ollari' + stress in this book returned 0 entries, so no Ollari-specific sentence is known to exist in it.
new_statements.identity_note: Krishnamurti 2003 (sec. 1.4 nos. 22-23) keeps 'Ollari (Hallari)' of Koraput district, Orissa (source Bhattacharya 1957) apart from 'Gadaba (Kondekor Gadaba)' of Srikakulam district, AP (source Bhaskararao 1980), while noting Burrow and Emeneau treat them as dialects of one language; the Kondekor/Konekor/Salur variety is Glottolog mudh1235 (Mudhili Gadaba), not pott1240. Bapuji 2019 is titled 'Ollari Gadaba'; the Shodhganga metadata gives no locality, so which variety it describes is unverified. The family-wide stress sentence quoted is not tied to any variety.

sources.note: Part One ch. 2 Phonology (A. Descriptive Phonology pp. 9-13: vowels incl. length/nasalization/diphthongs, single consonants, 2-consonant and 3+-consonant clusters; B. Sound-changes p. 14; C. Comparative Phonology pp. 15-18). Nothing on stress, accent, intonation or pitch anywhere in the book (a full-text search for stress/accent full scanned: zero hits). Closest remark: 'The long vowels occur mostly in monosyllabic words or in the first syllable of poly-syllabic words' (p. 9) — a vowel-length distribution statement, not a stress statement.
Segmental inventory only; nothing on stress. Supplied the Shodhganga handle for Bapuji 2019.
